Ellen — thanks for the clear asks. High level response (short checklist first, then brief notes):

Checklist (minimal acceptance set)
- artifact-manifest-v1.json — includes image checksum(s), artifact IDs, expected kernel/initramfs hashes, and signer metadata.
- signed-image-v1.sig — detached signature of the image bundle (Ed25519).
- cutover-checklist.pdf — operator steps and go/no-go gating criteria.

Operator/key ceremony expectations
- Your operator performs local manifest hash verification and validates signer fingerprints against the agreed KMS-derived registry (we provide the public key and fingerprint).
- If the site is fully isolated, we expect a single on-site operator to run the acceptance commands; for higher assurance you can require a two-person operator confirmation.

Emergency activation flow (fast path)
1) Operator receives artifact-manifest-v1.json + signed-image-v1.sig.
2) Run redwood-verify-manifest --manifest artifact-manifest-v1.json --sig signed-image-v1.sig 
3) If verification succeeds and checksum matches, run staged-activate --image-id <id> --rehearse false --rollback-tag <timestamp>.
4) If any verification step fails, invoke rollback and notify us via the emergency channel (ops@redwood.ai).

We've attached a draft manifest and the detached signature for your dry run. Also included a compact cutover checklist PDF that mirrors the steps above and includes expected exit codes for automation.

Open questions for us to confirm quickly:
- Acceptance window length you prefer for the emergency run? (we recommend 60 minutes for a single-image activation)
- Do you want us to provide a one-time operator token for the rehearsal or use your on-site keys?

I'm looping Naomi for the compliance trace and Ben/Monica for operator procedures and packaging.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
